e.summary: 德国罗伯特·科赫研究所发布的周度超额死亡率数据集：含周次日期与分组（如年龄组）等字段，以 CC-BY-4.0 许可发布于 Zenodo 并附 DOI，可正式引用；贡献者标明 ORCID 与所属部门，署名机构含德国联邦卫生部
e.summary_en: A weekly excess mortality dataset from Germany’s Robert Koch Institute, containing fields such as week date and group (for example age groups), released under CC-BY-4.0 on Zenodo with a DOI so it can be formally cited; contributors carry ORCID identifiers and departmental affiliations, and the attributing institutions include Germany’s Federal Ministry of Health
e.body:
**rki-excess-mortality** 是**德国罗伯特·科赫研究所（Robert Koch-Institut, RKI）发布的周度超额死亡率数据集**（仓库 `robert-koch-institut/Daten_des_Uebersterblichkeitsberichts`），**CC-BY-4.0 许可，实测 ★0、fork 0、主语言未标注、仓库体量 13,598 KB、创建于 2025-10-28、最后推送 2026-09-09**（**均 GitHub API 实测值**，**在解冻窗口内**）；**其 topics 逐字实测为 deutschland、epidemiologie、epidemiology、excess-mortality、germany、gesundheitsberichterstattung、mortalitaet、mortality、offene-daten、open-data、public-health-surveillance、rki、uebersterblichkeit**。

可核实信息（**均实测**）：**仓库描述逐字（德语）**说明：**该数据集提供德国**周度**超额死亡率数据，含**周次日期**与**相应分组**（例如年龄组）等信息**。**README 实测 15,117 字节**，**标题逐字为「Daten des Übersterblichkeitsberichts」**，**版面为带页眉区块的「Dokumentation」文档**；⭐ **署名逐字实测**：**「Robert Koch-Institut」**，**并列出五位**具名贡献者**，**每人附 **ORCID 标识****：**Benedikt Zacher**、**Andreas Hicketier**、**Alexander Ullrich**、**Michaela Diercke**、**Matthias an der Heiden**；**所属机构逐字实测为三处**：**¹ 德国联邦卫生部（Bundesministerium für Gesundheit, BMG）**、**² 罗伯特·科赫研究所 Fachgebiet 32**、**³ 罗伯特·科赫研究所 Fachgebiet 34**。⭐⭐ **其建议引用格式逐字实测（APA 风格）**：**「Robert Koch-Institut. (2026). Daten des Übersterblichkeitsberichts [Data set]. Zenodo. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22671600」**——**即这是一个**有 DOI、被要求按学术格式引用**的数据集**。⭐⭐ **该 DOI 经探活实测可解析**：**`https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22671600` 实测 HTTP 200、109.6KB、标题逐字为「Daten des Übersterblichkeitsberichts | Zenodo」**。

对 RIAA：**① ⭐⭐⭐ 「有 DOI、要求按 APA 引用」是本条目最重要的特征，也是它与同类数据的实质差别**——**超额死亡率数据的常见用法是「从某个网页抄一组数字」**，**而这份数据的发布形态是**可引用、可版本化的学术对象****；**对写论文、做行业报告或需要注明数据来源的学生，「怎么引」和「数字从哪来」一样重要**（**可与池内 [[excessmort]] 并读——**那是 CRAN 上的 R 方法包（0.8.2，周/日计数数据的弹性基线），提供的是**方法**；本条目提供的是**官方数据源**，两者互补而非重复****）。**② ⭐⭐ 「周度」粒度值得单独记一笔**——**超额死亡率通常按周或按月发布，而**周度**足以在事件进行中就看出异常**，**同时在统计上仍相对稳定**；**对做死亡率监测、寿险承保或巨灾后损失评估的学生，周度是「及时性 vs 噪声」之间的常用折中**（**本次未下载数据，故不转述其具体字段取值、覆盖年份或基线方法**）。**③ ⭐⭐ 「按年龄组等分组」说明该数据集不是单一总量**——**超额死亡率的分组结构决定了能否做**分年龄**分析**（**而分年龄正是寿险与年金的关切**）；**⚠️ 本次未核实其实际包含哪些分组维度与层级**。**④ ⭐⭐ 「贡献者逐一附 ORCID + 所属部门」是一种可核查的署名方式**——**ORCID 使每位贡献者可被唯一识别**，**这与池内 [[human-mortality-db]]、[[hmdhfdplus]] 所代表的死亡率数据基础设施相接**（**那些是跨国死亡率数据库，本条目是一个**单一国家的官方周度发布****）。**⑤ ⭐ 署名机构含**德国联邦卫生部**，说明该数据集的发布带有**政府卫生统计**性质**——**对做监管与官方统计研究的学生，「谁发布、谁的部门」本身是信息**（**⚠️ 该数据集与德国官方死亡统计（Destatis）的关系本次未核实**）。**⑥ ⭐ CC-BY-4.0 是一个**明确允许再利用（含商业用途）**的开放许可**——**对比本站收集到的多数 ★0 项目「无许可」或 `NOASSERTION`，这份数据的许可条件是清晰的**；**⚠️ 但**引用时仍须按其要求署名**，**故本词条建议读者直接使用其 DOI 与建议引用格式**。**⑦ ⭐ 可与池内其他官方死亡率/健康数据并读**：[[who-gho]]、[[ihme-gbd]]、[[cdc-wonder]]、[[eurostat]]、[[data-europa]]、[[oecd-insurance-data]]——**那几条是跨国的或他国的官方健康数据入口，本条目补的是**德国周度超额死亡率**这一具体发布**。

⚠️ **如实标注**：**①** 本次核实的是**仓库元数据、topics 十三项、仓库描述、README 的标题与署名区块（含五位贡献者的 ORCID 与三处所属机构）、建议引用格式逐字，以及其 DOI 的可解析性（HTTP 200、109.6KB、Zenodo 页面标题逐字）**，⭐ **但**未下载数据文件、未打开 Zenodo 记录页的正文、未读 README 其余部分（15,117 字节中的大部分）、未核实其字段字典与数据字典****，因此**不能转述其具体字段、覆盖年份、分组维度、基线计算方法、更新频率的精确值或数据体量**；**② ⭐⭐ 「周度」「含周次日期与分组（如年龄组）」来自**仓库描述**，**本次未核对数据本身**；**③ ⭐ **未核实**该数据集与 RKI 官方网站上超额死亡率报告的关系、以及两者是否为同一发布的不同渠道**；**④ ⭐ 该数据集涉及**人群死亡信息**——**其匿名化程度、是否属个人数据、以及再利用时的合规要求本次未评估**；**本词条**不主张**其可无条件用于任何用途**（**即使 CC-BY-4.0 允许再利用，署名与合规责任仍在使用者**）；**⑤ ⭐ 「CC-BY-4.0」为 GitHub API 实测的 SPDX 标识**，**本次未打开仓库内的 LICENSE 文件逐字核对**；**⑥ ⭐ 作者机构、RKI 的法定地位与统计口径本次未独立核实**（**均来自该数据集的自身文档**）；**⑦ ⭐ 本词条**不主张**该数据适用于精算定价或准备金评估**——**官方超额死亡率数据与**经调整的保险业死亡率表**是不同对象**；**⑧ 是否有中文材料本次未核实**（**README 实测为德语，建议引用格式为英文 APA**）。**核实说明**：`https://api.github.com/repos/robert-koch-institut/Daten_des_Uebersterblichkeitsberichts` 与 `/readme` 于 2026-09-11 经 GitHub API 实测读取（README 15,117 字节，标题、署名区块与建议引用格式逐字核对）；`https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22671600` 经 `discovery/probe-urls.sh` HTTP 200 实测（109.6KB）；**未下载数据、未打开 Zenodo 记录页正文、未读 README 其余部分**。

e.body_en:
**rki-excess-mortality** is **a weekly excess mortality dataset from Germany’s Robert Koch Institute (Robert Koch-Institut, RKI)** (repository `robert-koch-institut/Daten_des_Uebersterblichkeitsberichts`), **CC-BY-4.0 licensed, with measured ★0, 0 forks, no declared primary language, a 13,598 KB repository, created 2025-10-28 and last pushed 2026-09-09** (**all GitHub API measurements**, **inside the thaw window**); **its topics measurably read deutschland, epidemiologie, epidemiology, excess-mortality, germany, gesundheitsberichterstattung, mortalitaet, mortality, offene-daten, open-data, public-health-surveillance, rki and uebersterblichkeit**.

Verifiable details (**all measured**): **the repository description, verbatim in German**, states that **the dataset provides weekly excess mortality data for Germany, containing the week date and the respective group (for example age groups)**. **The README measures 15,117 bytes**, its **title verbatim "Daten des Übersterblichkeitsberichts"**, **laid out as a "Dokumentation" document with a header block**; ⭐ **the attribution reads verbatim "Robert Koch-Institut"**, **listing five named contributors each with an ORCID identifier**: **Benedikt Zacher**, **Andreas Hicketier**, **Alexander Ullrich**, **Michaela Diercke** and **Matthias an der Heiden**; **three affiliations read verbatim**: **¹ Germany’s Federal Ministry of Health (Bundesministerium für Gesundheit, BMG)**, **² Robert Koch-Institut, Fachgebiet 32** and **³ Robert Koch-Institut, Fachgebiet 34**. ⭐⭐ **Its suggested citation, verbatim in APA style**: **"Robert Koch-Institut. (2026). Daten des Übersterblichkeitsberichts [Data set]. Zenodo. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22671600"** — **a dataset with a DOI, intended to be cited academically**. ⭐⭐ **That DOI measurably resolves**: **`https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22671600` measured HTTP 200, 109.6KB, with the title verbatim "Daten des Übersterblichkeitsberichts | Zenodo"**.

For RIAA: **① ⭐⭐⭐ That it carries a DOI and an APA citation requirement is the entry’s most important feature and its substantive difference from comparable data** — **excess mortality data is commonly used by copying a set of numbers off a web page**, **whereas this is published as a citable, versionable academic object**; **for students writing papers or industry reports, "how do I cite it" matters as much as "where did the numbers come from"** (**readable with [[excessmort]] — that is a CRAN R methods package (0.8.2, flexible baselines for weekly and daily counts) offering the method, while this entry offers the official source; the two are complementary, not repetitive**). **② ⭐⭐ The weekly granularity deserves separate note** — **excess mortality is usually published weekly or monthly, and weekly is fine enough to show anomalies while an event is still unfolding while remaining statistically reasonably stable**; **for students monitoring mortality, underwriting life business or assessing post-catastrophe losses, weekly is the usual compromise between timeliness and noise** (**no data was downloaded, so specific field values, coverage years and baseline method are not restated**). **③ ⭐⭐ That it can be broken down by age group and similar groupings matters** — **the grouping structure determines whether age-specific analysis is possible**, **and age-specificity is precisely what life and annuity work cares about**; **⚠️ which grouping dimensions and levels it actually contains was not verified**. **④ ⭐⭐ Contributors each carrying an ORCID plus departmental affiliation is a checkable form of attribution** — **ORCID makes each contributor uniquely identifiable**; **this connects to the mortality data infrastructure represented by [[human-mortality-db]] and [[hmdhfdplus]]** (**those are cross-national mortality databases, whereas this is one country’s official weekly release**). **⑤ ⭐ The attributing institutions include Germany’s Federal Ministry of Health, giving the release the character of official government health statistics** — **for students of regulation and official statistics, who publishes and which department is itself information** (**⚠️ its relationship to Germany’s official death statistics (Destatis) was not verified**). **⑥ ⭐ CC-BY-4.0 is an open licence that clearly permits reuse including commercially** — **against the many ★0 projects in this corpus with no licence or `NOASSERTION`, this dataset’s terms are clear**; **⚠️ attribution is still required, so the entry advises using its DOI and suggested citation directly**. **⑦ ⭐ Readable with other official mortality and health data in the corpus**: [[who-gho]], [[ihme-gbd]], [[cdc-wonder]], [[eurostat]], [[data-europa]] and [[oecd-insurance-data]] — **those are cross-national or other countries’ official health data entry points, whereas this adds Germany’s weekly excess mortality release**.

⚠️ **Stated plainly**: **①** this check verified **the repository metadata, thirteen topics, the repository description, the README’s title and attribution block (including five contributors’ ORCIDs and three affiliations), the suggested citation verbatim, and its DOI’s resolvability (HTTP 200, 109.6KB, Zenodo page title verbatim)**, ⭐ **but downloaded no data file, opened no Zenodo record body, read only part of the README (of 15,117 bytes), and checked no field or data dictionary**, so **its specific fields, coverage years, grouping dimensions, baseline method, exact update frequency and data volume cannot be restated**; **② ⭐⭐ "Weekly" and "contains week date and group (for example age groups)" come from the repository description**, **not checked against the data itself**; **③ ⭐ Its relationship to the excess mortality reports on RKI’s own website, and whether the two are channels of the same release, were not verified**; **④ ⭐ The dataset concerns population mortality** — **its degree of anonymisation, whether it constitutes personal data, and the compliance requirements for reuse were not assessed**; **the entry does not claim it can be used unconditionally for any purpose** (**even where CC-BY-4.0 permits reuse, attribution and compliance remain the user’s responsibility**); **⑤ ⭐ "CC-BY-4.0" is the SPDX identifier measured via the GitHub API**, **and the LICENSE file inside the repository was not read verbatim**; **⑥ ⭐ The authoring institution, RKI’s legal status and its statistical basis were not independently verified** (**all come from the dataset’s own documentation**); **⑦ ⭐ The entry does not claim the data is suitable for actuarial pricing or reserving** — **official excess mortality data and adjusted insurance industry mortality tables are different objects**; **⑧ whether Chinese-language material exists was not verified** (**the README measurably is German, with an English APA citation format**). **Verification note**: `https://api.github.com/repos/robert-koch-institut/Daten_des_Uebersterblichkeitsberichts` and `/readme` were read via the GitHub API on 2026-09-11 (the 15,117-byte README with title, attribution block and suggested citation checked verbatim); `https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22671600` was probed at HTTP 200 (109.6KB); **no data downloaded, no Zenodo record body opened, rest of README unread**.
